1	# State of the Web 2020–2025: HTTP Archive Trends
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	
     5	HTTP Archive — State of the Web Report  
     6	https://httparchive.org/reports/state-of-the-web?start=2020_01_01&end=latest&view=list
     7	
     8	## Overview
     9	
    10	The HTTP Archive continuously crawls millions of URLs and records how the web is built. The "State of the Web" report tracks macro-level metrics including page weight, request counts, protocol adoption (HTTPS, HTTP/2, HTTP/3), TCP connection counts, and CSS best-practice adoption such as `font-display`. The data below covers January 2020 through early 2026, with desktop and mobile measured separately.
    11	
    12	## Sample Size
    13	
    14	The crawl sample has grown substantially. In January 2020 the desktop crawl covered roughly 5 million URLs and mobile roughly 3.5 million. By mid-2022 both lines jumped sharply — desktop reaching ~15 million and mobile ~10 million — before stabilizing around 16 million (desktop) and 12.5 million (mobile) by mid-2023 onward.
    15	
    16	![Timeseries of Sample Size — Desktop vs Mobile](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    17	
    18	## Page Weight & Requests
    19	
    20	Median total transfer size has risen gradually over five years. Desktop pages now weigh approximately 2,000 KB (median), up from ~1,600 KB in early 2020. Mobile pages track slightly lower but follow the same upward trend. The 75th-percentile desktop page exceeds 4,000 KB, indicating a long tail of heavy pages.
    21	
    22	![Timeseries of Total Kilobytes — Desktop vs Mobile with IQR bands](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    23	
    24	The median number of resources requested per page is 76 on desktop and 71 on mobile, each up roughly 3% over the observation period.
    25	
    26	| Metric | Desktop | Mobile | Desktop Δ | Mobile Δ |
    27	|---|---|---|---|---|
    28	| Total Kilobytes (median) | ~2,000 KB | ~1,900 KB | ▲ ~25% | ▲ ~25% |
    29	| Total Requests (median) | 76 | 71 | ▲ 2.7% | ▲ 2.9% |
    30	| TCP Connections / Page (median) | 12.0 | 11.0 | ▼ 14.3% | ▼ 26.7% |
    31	
    32	## TCP Connections Per Page
    33	
    34	Despite growing request counts, the median number of TCP connections per page has fallen — from about 15 (desktop) and 15 (mobile) in early 2020 to 12 and 11 respectively. This decline reflects the multiplexing benefits of HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, which allow many requests over fewer connections.
    35	
    36	![Timeseries of TCP Connections Per Page](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    37	
    38	## Protocol & Security Adoption
    39	
    40	### HTTPS
    41	
    42	HTTPS adoption is now effectively universal. 99.2% of desktop requests and 99.1% of mobile requests use HTTPS, representing an increase of roughly 19–20 percentage points since early 2020 when adoption was around 80%.
    43	
    44	### HTTP/2
    45	
    46	HTTP/2 accounts for 58.6% of desktop requests and 57.6% of mobile requests. Growth has been modest recently (1–3%), partly because HTTP/3 is absorbing some of the newer adoption.
    47	
    48	### HTTP/3 Support
    49	
    50	HTTP/3 support has seen explosive growth. Desktop support stands at 38.7% and mobile at 40.0%. The percentage increases from the 2020 baseline are enormous (reported as 38,600% desktop and 5,614% mobile) because the starting point was near zero. Note: HTTP Archive measures HTTP/3 *support* rather than actual usage because fresh Chrome instances default to HTTP/2 on first connection before discovering HTTP/3 capability via Alt-Svc headers.
    51	
    52	| Protocol Metric | Desktop | Mobile |
    53	|---|---|---|
    54	| HTTPS Requests | 99.2% | 99.1% |
    55	| HTTP/2 Requests | 58.6% | 57.6% |
    56	| HTTP/3 Support | 38.7% | 40.0% |
    57	
    58	## Font-Display Adoption
    59	
    60	The `font-display` CSS property helps avoid the Flash of Invisible Text (FOIT) during web font loading. As measured by Lighthouse, 40.1% of desktop pages and 42.5% of mobile pages now use this property — up 14.9% and 61.0% respectively since 2020. While adoption is growing, more than half of pages still risk FOIT.
    61	
    62	## Key Findings
    63	
    64	- **Page weight keeps climbing**: Median desktop pages now transfer ~2,000 KB, roughly 25% heavier than in 2020, driven by richer media and JavaScript.
    65	- **HTTPS is the new baseline**: At 99%+ of requests, unencrypted HTTP is essentially extinct on the modern web.
    66	- **HTTP/3 is the fastest-growing protocol metric**: From near-zero to ~40% support in under four years, HTTP/3 is rapidly becoming mainstream.
    67	- **Fewer TCP connections despite more requests**: Multiplexing in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 has cut median connections per page by 15–27%, improving network efficiency.
    68	- **Font-display still underused**: At ~40–42% adoption, there is significant room for improvement in avoiding invisible text during font loading.

   130	
   131	After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.

    13	## Consultant-specific Data Visualization Techniques
    14	
    15	### 1. KPI Dashboard Design
    16	
    17	KPI cards are the most common element in consulting reports. Standard layout (1280x720):
    18	
    19	```
    20	4-card layout: each card 280x180, gap 30
    21	  Card 1: x=45,  y=160
    22	  Card 2: x=355, y=160
    23	  Card 3: x=665, y=160
    24	  Card 4: x=975, y=160
    25	```
    26	
    27	**Card internal structure** (top to bottom):
    28	
    29	| Area | Content | Font Size | Style |
    30	|------|---------|-----------|-------|
    31	| Icon row | data-icon icon | 32x32 | Theme color |
    32	| Metric name | "Monthly Active Users" | 14px | Gray #64748B |
    33	| Core number | "1.2M" | 36-42px | Bold, dark color |
    34	| Trend annotation | "+12.3% vs last month" | 12px | Green=up / Red=down |
    35	
    36	**Trend arrow conventions**:
    37	- Up: `arrow-trend-up` icon + green text
    38	- Down: `arrow-trend-down` icon + red text
    39	- Flat: horizontal line icon + gray text
    40	
    41	### 2. Chart Color Conventions
    42	
    43	Consulting-style charts use **monochromatic depth gradients** rather than rainbow colors:
    44	
    45	```
    46	Primary series:   Theme color 100% opacity
    47	Comparison series: Theme color 60% opacity
    48	Baseline:         #94A3B8 (gray dashed line)
    49	Highlight:        Accent color (only for key data points)
    50	```
    51	
    52	### 3. Data Annotation Principles
    53	
    54	- **Direct data labels**: Place values at the top of bar charts — no legend needed
    55	- **Annotated trend lines**: Add text notes at key inflection points ("Policy change", "Product launch")
    56	- **Comparison baselines**: Mark industry average / target values with gray dashed lines
    57	- **Consistent units**: Maintain the same numeric units and precision within a chart
    58	
    59	### 4. Table Design
    60	
    61	Consulting reports frequently use tables for precise data:
    62	
    63	| Design Element | Specification |
    64	|----------------|---------------|
    65	| Header | Dark background + white text, font-weight="bold" |
    66	| Zebra striping | Alternate rows with `fill-opacity="0.05"` light background |
    67	| Number alignment | Numbers right-aligned, text left-aligned |
    68	| Highlighted row | Mark key rows with accent color `fill-opacity="0.1"` |
    69	| Borders | Use horizontal lines only to separate rows; avoid full grid lines |

    73	## Consulting-specific Layout Patterns
    74	
    75	### MECE Decomposition Tree
    76	
    77	Main trunk on the left, branches expanding rightward — mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive:
    78	
    79	```
    80	Main metric ──┬── Branch A (45%)
    81	              ├── Branch B (30%)
    82	              ├── Branch C (20%)
    83	              └── Branch D (5%)
    84	```
    85	
    86	- Use `<line>` to connect trunk to branches
    87	- Each branch has a `<rect>` container + percentage annotation
    88	- Sum must = 100% (or explicitly label "Other")
    89	
    90	### Driver Factor Tree
    91	
    92	Top-level metric → decomposed factors → actions. Ideal for performance attribution analysis:
    93	
    94	```
    95	Revenue growth 15%
    96	  ├── Average order value +8%  → Premium product line expansion
    97	  ├── Customer count +5%       → New channel acquisition
    98	  └── Repurchase rate +2%      → Loyalty program optimization
    99	```

   101	### Left-chart Right-text (Chart Interpretation)
   102	
   103	Core consulting report layout: chart on the left, key insights on the right:

   107	Insight area: x=780, y=120, w=460, h=480
   108	  - Core conclusion (bold, 16px)
   109	  - 3-5 bullet points (14px)
   110	  - Data source (12px, gray)

   117	### Page Titles

   120	
   121	| Type | Descriptive (avoid) | Assertion (recommended) |
   122	|------|---------------------|------------------------|
   123	| Market | "Market Overview" | "Domestic market grows 23% YoY, significantly outpacing global average" |
   124	| Competition | "Competitive Analysis" | "Three major competitors show clear weaknesses in channel coverage" |
   125	| Finance | "Financial Data" | "Gross margin improved for four consecutive quarters, breaking industry ceiling" |
   126	
   127	### Data Source Attribution
   128	
   129	Every data-containing page must include a source note at the bottom:
   130	
   131	```xml
   132	<text x="40" y="700" font-size="10" fill="#94A3B8">
   133	  Source: National Bureau of Statistics 2025 Annual Report; Internal team analysis
   134	</text>
   135	```
   136	
   137	### Key Takeaway Box
   138	
   139	Consulting-style content pages should include a **Takeaway Box** below the title:
   140	
   141	```
   142	Position: x=40, y=80, w=1200, h=50
   143	Background: Light theme color (fill-opacity="0.08")
   144	Text: 14-16px, one-sentence summary of the page's core takeaway
   145	```

   148	
   149	## Speaker Notes Style
   150	
   151	### Narrative Tone
   152	
   153	Consultant-style speaker notes use a **conclusion-driven** approach — state the conclusion first, then present supporting evidence. Professional, concise, and persuasive tone.
   154	
   155	### Stage Direction Markers
   156	
   157	| Marker | Purpose | Example |
   158	|--------|---------|---------|
   159	| `[Pause]` | Silence after key conclusions, let the audience absorb | "This means our market share is being eroded. [Pause]" |
   160	| `[Data]` | Cue to verbalize numbers conversationally | "[Data] 85% → more than eight out of ten customers reported this issue" |
   161	| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, must be at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Based on that analysis, let's look at specific recommendations." |
   162	
   163	### Notes Writing Guidelines
   164	
   165	- **Conclusion first**: The first sentence of each page's notes is the core takeaway
   166	- **Conversational data**: 30% → "roughly one-third", 85% → "more than eight out of ten", 2.5x → "two and a half times"
   167	- **Evidence follows immediately**: After the conclusion, provide 2-3 supporting data points/facts
   168	- **Professional terminology**: Use terms like "insight", "driver", "key lever" etc.
   169	- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core conclusion (2) Supporting data (3) Next steps`
   170	
   171	### Notes Example
   172	
   173	```markdown
   174	# 03_key_findings
   175	
   176	[Transition] Based on our market scan, we have distilled three key findings.
   177	
   178	First, the primary growth driver is shifting from acquisition to retention.
   179	[Data] New customer acquisition cost rose nearly 40% year-over-year, yet improved repurchase rates contributed over 60% of revenue growth. [Pause]
   180	
   181	Second, lower-tier market growth significantly outpaces tier-1 and tier-2 cities.
   182	Third, the 25-35 female user segment has an ARPU 1.8x the overall average.
   183	
   184	Key points: (1) Growth engine shifting from acquisition to retention (2) Lower-tier market opportunity window (3) High-value user persona
   185	Duration: 2 minutes
   186	```

     7	## 1. SVG Banned Features Blacklist

    16	| `class` | CSS selector attributes (`id` inside `<defs>` is a legitimate reference and is NOT banned) |

    18	| `<foreignObject>` | Embedded external content |

    20	| `textPath` | Text along a path |
    21	| `@font-face` | Custom font declarations |
    22	| `<animate*>` / `<set>` | SVG animations |
    23	| `<script>` / event attributes | Scripts and interactivity |

   107	
   108	## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques
   109	
   110	> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).
   111	
   112	### Shadow
   113	
   114	#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended
   115	
   116	Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.
   117	
   118	```xml
   119	<defs>
   120	  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
   121	    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
   122	    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
   123	    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
   124	    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
   125	    <feMerge>
   126	      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
   127	      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
   128	    </feMerge>
   129	  </filter>
   130	</defs>
   131	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
   132	```
   133	
   134	Recommended parameters:
   135	```
   136	stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
   137	flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
   138	dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
   139	dx:             0–2
   140	```
   141	
   142	#### Colored Shadow
   143	
   144	Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.
   145	
   146	```xml
   147	<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
   148	  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
   149	  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
   150	  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
   151	  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
   152	  <feMerge>
   153	    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
   154	    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
   155	  </feMerge>
   156	</filter>
   157	```
   158	
   159	Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.
   160	
   161	#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback
   162	
   163	Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:
   164	
   165	```xml
   166	<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
   167	<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
   168	<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
   169	<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
   170	<!-- Main card -->
   171	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
   172	```
   173	
   174	### Image Overlay
   175	
   176	#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common
   177	
   178	Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).
   179	
   180	```xml
   181	<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
   182	<defs>
   183	  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
   184	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
   185	    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
   186	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
   187	  </linearGradient>
   188	</defs>
   189	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
   190	```
   191	
   192	#### Bottom Gradient Bar
   193	
   194	Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.
   195	
   196	```xml
   197	<defs>
   198	  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
   199	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
   200	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>

## III. Visual Theme
